items.title: Eligible bounties tab, and a new bounty on an existing list
items.body:
## What's new

- **Eligible for me to claim.** The Bounties screen has two tabs: House bounties and Eligible for me to claim. The Eligible tab lists the open bounties you qualify for, read from the instance's `GET /api/bounties/eligible`, each with a "you qualify — rank X ≥ Y" chip. It hides your own bounties and ones whose auto-pay minimum your rank doesn't meet. Every account can claim from it, the issuer included.
- **New bounty on this list.** The issuer can add another bounty to an existing list from the bounty's detail pane, with no new list published.
- **Safer creates.** After a create times out, a second Enter on the same list is refused while a new bounty has appeared there, so one intent never pays twice. The check is kept per list and survives closing and reopening the form and switching accounts.

## Checks

- `mbx nextest run`: 115 passed.
- e2e on the cua box: scenario S (new bounty on a list) and T (eligible list across an account switch mid-request) pass.

items.title: [#873] Add deterministic stalled-bounty diagnostics
items.body:
## What

Versioned diagnostic that gives every claimed or submitted bounty **one exact recovery action** before claim or verification deadlines strand solver work and escrow.

## Acceptance criteria coverage

| Criterion in #873 | Where |
|---|---|
| Versioned diagnostic from canonical lifecycle events and immutable windows | `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `DEFAULT_WINDOWS` |
| Classify healthy claimed / claim-expiring / submitted / verification-expiring / verifier-unavailable / settled / terminal | `classify()`; `ClassifyTests` |
| One deterministic next action and deadline for every non-terminal stalled item | `next_action_for()`; `resolve_deadline()`; `test_every_non_terminal_item_has_one_action_and_deadline` |
| Never infer acceptance, rejection or payment from GitHub state, a tx hash or an AI opinion | `PaymentInferenceTests`: a `TransactionBroadcast` never sets `settled`; only canonical `BountySettled` does |
| Fixtures for boundary timestamps, missing terms, stale index data, verifier outage, already settled work | `BoundaryTests`, `MissingTermsTests`, `StaleIndexTests`, `VerifierOutageTests`, `PaymentInferenceTests` |

## Immutable benchmark

`python3 benchmarks/direct-inventory-v1/stalled-work/check.py` — **passed**, 21 tests, exit 0.

## Design note

`resolve_deadline()` falls back to an immutable window anchored at the observed lifecycle timestamp when a row omits its own deadline, so the "one deadline per non-terminal item" guarantee holds even for incomplete rows. A row with genuinely no terms is flagged `missing_terms` rather than being assigned a guessed deadline.

## Note

A PR, a test result, or a verifier response is not payment evidence; only canonical `BountySettled` proves payment.

items.body:
## Description

Funding a bounty currently requires the Stellar CLI.

## Tasks

- Add `/new`: a form for finding reference, amount (XLM), and deadline (date picker, at most 1 year)

items.title: [#686] Add a concise direct-bounty evidence checklist
items.body:
## What

Adds a concise, machine-readable evidence checklist for direct coding bounties.

It binds four things and keeps three kinds of evidence in three separate buckets:

- **submission** — what was delivered: `repository`, `source_commit`, `subdirectory`, `pull_request_url`, `artifact_url`, `artifact_sha256`
- **verification** — what checked it: `check_run_urls`
- **payment** — what paid: canonical settlement receipt **only**

## Acceptance criteria coverage

| Criterion in #686 | Where |
|---|---|
| Binds exact source commit, repository, subdirectory, PR URL, check-run URLs, artifact digest | `REQUIRED_FIELDS` + `_validate_submission` / `_validate_verification` |
| Separates submission, verification, payment evidence | three top-level keys in the returned payload |
| Rejects empty, mutable, or non-HTTPS artifact references | `_reject_mutable` (rejects `/latest`, `/main/`, `/HEAD/`, `?ref=main`, `@main`, `branch=`), `_is_https_url` |
| Output compact enough for an MCP or API response, no secrets or personal data | `_scrub` drops keys matching token/secret/password/api_key/private_key/seed/mnemonic/email/author/maintainer/wallet/address/cookie/session/credential |

## The payment boundary

Local input can never assert payment. A `settled: true` in caller-side state is reported as `unverified`, because that is precisely the claim being checked. Settled requires all four: `provenance == "canonical_live"`, `tx_hash` (`0x` + 64 hex), `log_key`, positive integer `block_number`. A bare transaction hash is not a settlement event.

This mirrors `.openhands/hooks/agent-bounties-evidence.py` on purpose — the same rule, defence in depth rather than one line in one place.

## Tests

`python3 crates/sdk-python/tests/test_direct_evidence_checklist.py`

18 tests, all passing. Offline, replayable, no network / clock / randomness, exits 0. Covers: passing evidence, every missing required field, empty string treated as missing, mutable artifact URLs, non-HTTPS schemes (`http`, `file`, `git`, `ftp`), branch names as commits, short commits, malformed PR URLs, empty / duplicate / non-HTTPS check runs, subdirectory traversal, local `settled` flag staying unverified, five malformed settlement receipts, canonical receipt settling, secret scrubbing, output determinism, binding-digest coverage, and non-mapping input.

## Note

A PR, a test result, or a verifier response is not payment evidence. Only canonical `BountySettled` proves payment.

items.body:
## Summary
- Pre-register a bounded feasibility spike for wildcard bounty #304.
- Add a dependency-free region-capability model and six tests for transfer, aliases, aggregates, branch joins, missing call summaries, and distinct allocation identities.
- Map 26 current corpus cases to region/capability behavior and record semantic gaps.

## Evidence
- Standalone model: `rustc --edition=2021 --test spikes/spike11-region-capabilities/region_model.rs` — 6 passed, 0 failed with local Rust 1.90.0.
- Based on latest main `b73ce2fc485df6711b8e4cb21893fe547bd04878`; the 45-file corpus was checked after rebasing.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- QA found caller-supplied region IDs could collide; the model now generates distinct IDs across states and has a regression test. The PR branch history has been rewritten from latest main and no longer retains a generated PDB artifact.

## Scope and acceptance status
This is a research spike only; it does not change the compiler. The 26-case table is a manual semantic mapping, not executable corpus encoding, so it does not satisfy the bounty's 24-case encoding gate. It does not measure the >20% manual-wiring threshold or establish the integrated <250 LOC target. The host lacks the repository-pinned Rust 1.99.0 and `rustfmt`; `make test-quick` was not run. No bounty claim is made.

The narrow result is that capability transfer can invalidate aliases in a small model, while region provenance still needs to propagate through aggregates, calls, closures, and control-flow joins. Please treat this as an evidence artifact for deciding whether a fuller prototype is worth pursuing.

items.title: Keep the entered bounty amount as the solver reward
items.body:
## What Changed

Entering 100 USDC with a 10 USDC verifier reward previously produced a 90 USDC solver reward. The entered amount now stays at 100; verification is added separately, and review shows the full funding total and protocol fees. Existing fee calculations and contracts are unchanged.

New briefs store an explicit solver reward. Legacy briefs preserve their staged allocation: a saved 20 USDC total with 2 USDC verification restores 18 for the solver even when the hidden manual form still contains its 0.10 default. Missing or invalid staged allocation requires a new reward choice. Explicit reward edits remain authoritative. Assistant and WebMCP staging reject proposals that change the stated solver reward, including proposals with a new operation ID. Saved sessions retain approval binding and restoration behavior.

## Linked Bounty Or Issue

Owner-requested correction; no linked bounty or issue. No payout or settlement is claimed.

## Maintainer Change Notice

This PR records the implementation scope; no separate notice or reviewer request was sent. Relevant open PRs were inspected before editing. Coordinate overlapping composer changes with the autonomous-v2 integration before merge and preserve its existing 7.5% fee formula. This public-main baseline uses the legacy zero-fee contract, so its regression total is 100 + 10 = 110. It does not activate another protocol or introduce a new fee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Entered solver reward survives preparation, review and reload.
- [x] Verification is additional and displayed separately.
- [x] Assistant staging cannot silently reduce the reward.
- [x] Legacy allocation survives restoration and unrelated edits; actual reward edits invalidate the proposal.
- [x] Contract fees and settlement behavior remain unchanged.

## Validation

At `a1b1c32068696007620faf71b6a04daa80c48601`:

- Core preflight and diff checks passed.
- The staged-allocation repair matches the independently reviewed three-file patch byte for byte. Its two regression paths failed before the fix (19.9 instead of 18); the repaired posting-brief, creator-review/workspace, saved-session and WebMCP suite passed 142/142 tests.
- The complete posting browser regression suite passed after integration, including desktop/mobile 100 solver + 10 verification, reload, unrelated edits, approval recovery and rejection of imported proposals that reduce the reward.
- Site checks passed, including 118 checks in their Node suite.
- The separate manual-entry browser test was updated from the obsolete deducted-reward expectation. Mobile (390px) and desktop (1440px) now pass with the explicit breakdown 20.01 solver + 0.11 verification = 20.12 total.
- An independent review of all 14 changed files at this exact head found no blocking source findings. The fixed P1 discussion is resolved. This source review does not substitute for GitHub's required independent approval identity.
- All six latest-head GitHub workflows passed, including CI (full-check, postgres-sync, sdlc-recovery and ruleset-drift), Containers, Dependency Review, Code Size Report and both verifier workflows. Required latest-push independent GitHub approval remains outstanding.

Earlier validation at the preceding head included 175 targeted tests, 107 affected staging tests after strengthening the operation-ID guard, and six successful GitHub workflows. Current integration evidence is retained in the owner's `verification-20261021` workspace.

## SDLC And Recovery

R3 payment-amount presentation change. The saved brief and approved draft remain authoritative; funding still uses the protocol transaction. Failure cases include legacy-total reinterpretation, hidden-form allocation drift, stale approval and cross-device changes. Existing immutable draft hashes preserve review binding. Rollback is a commit revert, retaining legacy-field read compatibility. Posting layout and recovery tests are the health checks.

## Release Status

Ready for review; not merged or deployed. Requires the normal maintainer review and coordination with the overlapping protocol integration. No live payment was executed.
